caveats:
Pixel values are the source's native int16 representation, scaled x10 (raw value / 10 = true
Mg/ha). This scale factor is recorded in each resource's GeoTIFF band metadata (Scale/Offset
tags), but most plain script-based reads (e.g. a bare rasterio `.read()` or GDAL
`ReadAsArray()` call) do not apply it automatically and will return values 10x too high unless
you divide by 10 (or apply the Scale tag) yourself.
methodology_other:
CTrees produces its aboveground biomass (AGB) estimates by combining light detection and
ranging (LiDAR) measurements from NASA's ICESat and GEDI satellites -- which provide a global
dataset of vegetation structure and aboveground live biomass, calibrated against more than 1.5
million ground plot data points -- with change-detection machine learning algorithms customized
for more than 800 ecoregions globally, using satellite radar and optical imagery to map biomass
and biomass change annually.

This HDX dataset provides only the AGB layer. CTrees' broader Land Carbon Map product (see
https://ctrees.org/products) also estimates belowground biomass (via ecological models) and
per-pixel uncertainty (via error propagation models); neither is included in this dataset.

Peer-reviewed methodology references: Saatchi, S., et al. (2011). Benchmark map of forest carbon
stocks in tropical regions across three continents. PNAS, 108(24), 9899-9904.
https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1019576108. Xu, L., et al. (2021). Changes in global terrestrial live
biomass over the 21st century. Science Advances, 7(27), eabe9829.
https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abe9829.
name: mli-ctrees-aboveground-biomass
notes:
This dataset contains annual, 100m-resolution above ground biomass (AGB) estimates from CTrees,
a NASA-affiliated forest-carbon monitoring organization, clipped to this country's boundary from
CTrees' global AGB raster.

Pixel values are stored as int16, scaled x10 relative to the true value in megagrams per
hectare (Mg/ha) -- divide by 10 to get Mg/ha. See the caveats field and resource description
for details on how this scale factor is recorded and why it isn't applied automatically by most
tools.

organization.description:
CTrees is a U.S.-based science and technology 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that has developed the first global system to monitor, report, and verify (MRV) carbon stocks and land-use activities for every ecosystem on land.

Founded in 2022, CTrees was created by scientists to bridge the gap between science and technology innovation and the data needs of policy and markets. Today, our trusted, independent data is used by leading governments and organizations to measure the impact of programs and projects worldwide.

For access to the full Above Ground Biomass data set, including global data from 2001 to 2025, email Janet Smith at jsmith@ctrees.org.
